high_level_description: Wordless narrative embroidery inspired by the Bayeux Tapestry: three successive registers follow one sealed blue workflow band from authoring through a fixed execution loom to completed output, while a red revision stays rolled aside for a future run; flat profile figures, linen ground, wool outlines, no inscriptions or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: An undyed linen field is divided into three stacked horizontal registers by narrow stitched bands of leaves and ordinary workshop animals. The upper register is for preparation, the middle for execution, and the lower for completion. Every register remains part of one continuous cloth. No Latin inscription, alphabetic mark, numeral, caption, heraldic emblem, pointing hand, or arrow appears.

elements.desc: Single continuous blue wool workflow band crossing all three registers with rounded ends and no pointed tip. One author binds its upper end around a plain seal; the unchanged middle section sits inside the loom's fixed wooden guide; the lower end emerges beside the finished object. No branch joins it during execution.

Workflow author shown in flat profile, medium-brown skin, short dark curls, cream tunic, indigo mantle, ochre shoes, and a concentrated expression. Kneeling in the upper register, they close a plain circular seal around the blue band's rounded starting end with a wooden press, without touching the separate revision material below.

Fixed execution loom occupying the middle register, constructed from ochre timber with three immovable guide slots, a weighted crossbar, and one sealed side latch. Its mechanism accepts the prepared band at the top and produces one bounded woven panel below; no spare slot, movable branch, writing surface, or discretionary control is present.

Execution worker shown in flat profile, dark skin, close-cropped black hair, indigo tunic, cream leggings, red shoes, and a steady neutral expression. Standing beside the loom in the middle register, he turns its single wooden crank with both hands and follows the fixed mechanism without altering the sealed guide.

Completed repair panel resting in the lower register, woven as one compact cream rectangle with a blue border and three purely pictorial tool shapes. Its edges are finished and its material visibly continues from the unchanged blue workflow band; the panel contains no words, numbers, badges, seals, or directional symbols.

Separate red wool revision roll resting unopened in a shallow basket at the far right of the lower register. The roll has rounded ends, a plain cream binding cord, and one altered woven junction visible at its edge. It remains physically disconnected from the operating loom and the completed blue-band output.
